item.title: Vunato dump fire enters fourth day as residents call for its relocation
item.description: Residents in Lautoka have been enduring smoke from fires at the Vunato Rubbish Dump for the past 10 to 15 years, with the Lautoka Ratepayers Association calling on the Government to urgently address the recurring problem. item.content:encoded:
Residents in Lautoka have been enduring smoke from fires at the Vunato Rubbish Dump for the past 10 to 15 years, with the Lautoka Ratepayers Association calling on the Government to urgently address the recurring problem.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Lautoka resident and Ratepayers Association President Narayan Reddy says this is the fourth day of the latest fire, with residents continuing to suffer from smoke spreading from the rubbish dump.

Reddy says the dump has been catching fire almost every year, with incidents often occurring after the free clean-up campaign.

He says the fires normally burn for about a week, with last year's fire only being brought under control with the help of rain.

Reddy says although the Lautoka City Council built lookout points and installed water hydrants following last year's fire, these measures have done little to prevent or control the recurring fires.

He says residents have been calling for the rubbish dump to be relocated, with a Lautoka businessman offering 46 acres of land earlier this year for the proposed relocation.

Reddy says the Lautoka Ratepayers Association had written to the Lautoka City Council and the Minister for Local Government regarding the land offer but had not received a response from either party.

The Association is now calling on the Government to look into the recurring fires, saying residents are suffering from the smoke.

It is also requesting the National Fire Authority to assist the Lautoka City Council in fighting the fire and bringing it under control more quickly.

The $57.4 million economic contribution from international yacht visitors in 2025 is expected to benefit Fijian businesses and communities, with Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Tourism and Civil Aviation Viliame Gavoka revealing that 824 international yachts visited the country, generating $52 million in direct visitor expenditure.

Gavoka highlighted this in Parliament while responding to a question from MP Sakiusa Tubuna on the Ministry's coordination with relevant agencies to address yacht clearance and administrative issues raised by the yachting sector.
